title: Localization away in an algebra commutes with arbitrary base change
statement: Let $R,A,B$ be commutative rings with ring homomorphisms $R\to A$ and $R\to B$, and let $g\in A$. Write $A_g$ for localization at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. For commutative $R$-algebras $C,D$, $C\otimes_R D$ denotes their tensor product algebra [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], whose multiplication is $(c\otimes d)(c'\otimes d')=cc'\otimes dd'$ and whose unit is $1\otimes1$. Put $T=A\otimes_R B$ and $\bar g=g\otimes1\in T$. There is a canonical isomorphism of $B$-algebras $A_g\otimes_R B\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{\bar g}$ which sends $(a/g^n)\otimes b$ to $(a\otimes b)/\bar g^n$ for every $a\in A$, $b\in B$ and integer $n\ge0$.
